We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts list. Need number of methyl groups (CH3). Methyl carbons appear around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, also maybe 20-30. In list we have 26.40, 36.40 (two same), 58.70, plus aromatic carbons (130-168). So likely methyl is 26.40 ppm. Also 36.40 could be methylene or tertiary carbon. 58.70 likely carbon attached to O (e.g., O-CH3). O-CH3 appears around 55-60 ppm. That could be a methoxy group (CH3 attached to O). So that is also a methyl carbon. So total methyl groups: 2 (one aliphatic methyl, one methoxy). Need confirm if any other methyls hidden: 36.40 duplicates maybe two equivalent carbons (maybe two CH2). Not methyl. So answer 2.

Check if any other data needed. Could also use proton NMR to confirm. Let's get proton NMR.
